newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM, NORTHWEST TO RAISE FARES. [CORRECTED 01:17 GMT 20/12]
newsitem.headline: KLM, NORTHWEST TO RAISE FARES. [CORRECTED 01:17 GMT 20/12]

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday it would hike its passenger tariffs ex-Netherlands from Wednesday.

"Based on industrial consultations within the IATA framework and in line with a number of major IATA carriers, KLM and its partner airline Northwest Airlines have decided to raise flight tariffs in the Netherlands market with effect from December 18," KLM said in a statement.
KLM said its Cargo division would hike its tariffs in the first quarter of 1997, depending on prevailing market conditions.
"The rise in cargo tariffs will be in the order of five to 10 percent," it said.
It added that it would withdraw the fuel surcharge on passenger fares with the introduction of the fare increases, but said the fuel surcharge on cargo would remain in place.

(Corrects above para from "It added that it would scrap its current fuel surcharge on passenger fares and freight with the introduction of the higher tariffs", making clear cargo fuel surcharge remains).
"Depending on local market conditions, the tariffs applied by KLM in foreign markets will be raised by an average five percent," KLM said.
Fares from the Netherlands to the Middle East would go up by four percent, while flights to Brazil would rise by three percent.
Fares to other destinations would rise by five percent, with the exception of the United States, where the five percent fare increase came into effect on November 12, KLM said.
Lowest-fare tariffs to Australia and New Zealand were exempt from the fare hike, it said.
